subject: botfly and mosquito
title: This Fly Catches a Mosquito in Mid-Air and Loads It With Eggs

scenes.text: This fly hunts mosquitoes. Not to eat them.
The human botfly of Central and South America grabs a mosquito in mid-air, and sticks her own eggs onto it.
When that mosquito lands on a warm animal to feed, the warmth makes the eggs hatch.
The larvae slip in through the bite, or a hair follicle, and live under the skin for five to twelve weeks.
Over forty kinds of mosquitoes and flies are known carriers. The botfly just needs something that already knows how to find skin.

description:
The human botfly, Dermatobia hominis, does not lay its eggs on a host. It catches a mosquito in flight, attaches its eggs to the mosquito's body and releases it.
When the mosquito feeds on a warm-blooded animal, the change in temperature makes the eggs hatch and the larvae enter the skin through the bite wound or a hair follicle, where they develop for five to twelve weeks. More than 40 species of mosquitoes and other flies are known carriers. The botfly ranges from Mexico to northern Argentina.
Which parasite has the cleverest delivery system? Comment below.
first_comment: The adult botfly is 12 to 18 millimetres long and never eats. Which is worse: the botfly or the mosquito it uses?
